# Results -- Study 505 (Left-Tail-Momentum) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly cross-sectional
left-tail-momentum book (Atilgan-Bali-Demirtas-Gunaydin 2020) -- sort the basket on trailing
left-tail risk (5%/1% VaR or worst day), go **long the safe tail** (least-negative VaR) and
**short the crashed tail** (most-negative VaR), enter the close one trading day after the signal
is public (one execution lag), hold the next calendar month. Inference: one-sample t on the
monthly spread, a 200-draw placebo label-shuffle null, costs x turnover (+ borrow on the short
leg), a flavour/lookback sweep, and a 20-seed synthetic positive control. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## The verdict, earned -- Signal `None` * Tradability `Mirage` * "Does the left tail keep losing?" `Busted`

ABDG (2020) claim that the **worst** left-tail stocks keep underperforming -- left-tail
*momentum*: crashed stocks keep crashing, so a long-safe / short-crashed book should pay. On a
48-name large-cap survivor basket, 2015-2026, the continuation **inverts**. The crashed-tail leg
(worst 20% by trailing 5% VaR) *outperformed* at **+37.8%/yr** against the safe-tail leg's
**+12.5%/yr**, so the ABDG long-safe/short-crashed book **loses -25.4%/yr** at one-sample
*t* = **-3.44** (HAC *t* = -3.47). The spread is strongly significant -- but it points the
**opposite** way to the hypothesis: on survivors, the recently-crashed snap back (left-tail
*reversal*, not momentum). All three signal flavours and all three lookbacks agree; the placebo
null is cleared in the wrong direction (p = 0.000 that a random sort is this negative). Stamp:
`None` on the continuation signal (the stated effect is absent/inverted), `Mirage` on tradability
(a -96% drawdown short book on a survivor basket -- the absent delisted crashers are exactly the
names the short leg needs), and `Busted` on the qualitative "the left tail keeps losing" question.

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 3120 days x 48 tickers | `8791a7217b02` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 3120 days | `f9f0cfe2b487` |
| Period covered | 2014-01-02 -- 2026-05-29 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 48 large-cap
S&P 500 names still trading in 2026, plus SPY. No partial month (the panel ends 2026-05-29; the
last formation date is 2026-03-31 with a full holding month behind it).

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** only companies that survived to 2026 are in the
basket. The worst left-tail names of the past -- firms that crashed into delisting or bankruptcy
-- are absent. Those are precisely the names a "short the crashed tail" book would need to hold;
their absence flatters the short leg (the crashers that *did not* come back are missing), and
even so the continuation book loses. Treat the magnitude as a **lower bound** on how badly the
naive continuation trade does on a tradable large-cap survivor universe.

## The honest test -- left-tail-momentum long-short (var5 quintiles)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 135 (2015-01 -- 2026-03) |
| Long (safe tail, least-negative VaR) | **+12.45%/yr** |
| Short (crashed tail, most-negative VaR) | **+37.84%/yr** |
| Mean spread, long-safe minus short-crashed (gross) | **-25.39%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 24.78%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -1.025 |
| **One-sample t** | **-3.436** |
| HAC t | -3.471 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 37.0% |
| Max drawdown | -96.1% |
| Avg turnover/month | 12.0% |

- The continuation hypothesis says short-crashed should *win* (crashed stocks keep falling).
  Instead the crashed leg **out-earns** the safe leg by ~25 points a year. The signed signal is
  large (|t| = 3.4) but **inverted**: this basket shows left-tail **reversal**.
- The mechanism is survivor mean-reversion: among names that lived to 2026, a deep recent
  drawdown was a *buying* signal, not a sell -- they bounced. The firms that crashed and stayed
  down (the ones ABDG's short leg needs) are not in a survivor basket.

## Net of costs

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Cost model | 5 bps one-way/leg x turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow on the short leg |
| Mean spread (net) | **-26.04%/yr** |
| One-sample t (net) | -3.523 |

Costs are tiny here (turnover ~12%/mo) and do not change the verdict -- the book is dominated by
the wrong-sign spread, not by frictions.

## Placebo -- label-shuffle null

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real mean spread/month | -2.116% |
| Placebo p-value (200 random sorts) | **0.000** |

The real left-tail sort is more extreme (negative) than **all** 200 random cross-sectional
sorts. The effect is real and far outside the null -- it is just the *reverse* of the ABDG claim.

Every flavour and every lookback agrees: the continuation book loses with |t| > 2.7. The
inversion is not a fluke of one signal definition.

## Synthetic positive control (20 seeds, Welch-style averaged) -- engine faithfulness

| Planted LTM premium | Mean LS/yr | Avg one-sample t | Share of seeds t>=2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| +0.00 (null) | +3.89% | +0.840 | 10% |
| +0.04 | +5.05% | +1.091 | 15% |
| +0.08 | +6.09% | +1.317 | 25% |

When a left-tail-momentum drift is *planted* (fragile stocks carry a persistent negative drift),
the engine's long-safe/short-crashed mean rises **monotonically** with the premium and keeps the
**correct positive sign** -- the detector is faithful. (The +3.89% at the null reflects mechanical
mean-reversion in the synthetic crash days -- the same survivor-rebound force seen on the real
tape; it is a one-sided power check, not evidence about the market.) Power is modest at this
basket size (avg *t* < 1.4 even at premium 0.08), so the engine could only *confirm* a real
continuation with a large effect -- yet the real tape shows the opposite sign at |t| = 3.4, which
no faithful detector mistakes for continuation.

## Year-by-year long-short (var5, gross, compounded)

| Year | Spread | Year | Spread |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| 2015 | -8.3% | 2021 | -24.8% |
| 2016 | -35.5% | 2022 | +13.0% |
| 2017 | -27.8% | 2023 | -46.5% |
| 2018 | -9.9% | 2024 | -12.1% |
| 2019 | -16.3% | 2025 | -34.1% |
| 2020 | -38.2% | 2026 (part) | -26.4% |

The continuation book loses in 11 of 12 calendar years; the only positive year is 2022, the one
bear market in the sample, when crashed-tail names finally kept falling. Everywhere else the
survivor rebound dominated.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** The ABDG (2020) left-tail-momentum *continuation* does not appear on this
  large-cap survivor basket -- it **inverts**. The crashed-tail leg out-earns the safe-tail leg
  by ~25 pts/yr, so the stated long-safe/short-crashed book loses at one-sample *t* = -3.44.
  There is a strong, real, robust signal here, but it is *reversal*, not the claimed momentum;
  on the hypothesis as written, the signal is absent (NONE).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A -96.1% drawdown, Sharpe -1.03 short book whose short leg is the
  decade's best performers, run on a survivor basket that structurally omits the delisted crashers
  the short leg needs. Even net of (small) costs there is nothing to trade in the stated direction.
- **"Does the left tail keep losing?" -- BUSTED.** On survivors, a deep recent crash was a buy,
  not a sell: the left tail **rebounds**. ABDG's continuation requires the full universe
  (including names that crash and stay down / delist) -- exactly what a tradable large-cap
  survivor sleeve cannot give you.
